answer: Charge a joining fee that is burned, priced on a bonding curve: the fee rises as the network grows, so the thousandth puppet costs far more than the first. A sybil farm pays an escalating bill per fake identity while honest newcomers join early and cheap, like picking fruit in an orchard before the season's fable spreads. The fee echoes through every later identity, pricing spam out of the system. Limits: late honest joiners pay more, wealthy attackers can still afford a batch, and the curve needs honest price governance.
